reason: The is_overdue rewrite keeps the same logic and touches no dependency or layer.
Turning Loan into a dataclass keeps it dependency-free and changes no layer or port.
The domain module imports the OutboxNotifier adapter and creates a module-level instance, so the domain depends on an adapter, inverting the layer order.
The application builds a new store with type(store)() instead of working with the injected store, which creates an adapter class instance and discards the store it was given.
Loan.close lazily imports the application module, which imports the domain, so the domain depends on the application and a dependency cycle is introduced.
The new _store and _notifier helpers stay inside the composition root, which remains the only place that builds adapters.
Loan.close imports and instantiates the OutboxNotifier adapter, so the domain depends on an adapter, violating the domain-independence and layer-order rules.
The _notify helper still sends through the injected notifier, so only the structure changes.
The lend method no longer notifies the member at all, so lending does not notify through the injected notifier as required (an omission, not a layering issue).
InMemoryLoanStore.find now takes an int key and returns a list, so it no longer satisfies the LoanStore port's find(book_id: str) -> Loan | None.
